description: Somos Los Enredados, una dupla de Ingeniería Mecatrónica e Industrial de Nicaragua participando en 'Flame in Freefall'. Desarrollamos un Gemelo Digital co-simulado para detección temprana y contención de incendios en microgravedad, integrando SolidWorks y diseño electrónico/PCB en kiCAD y Python (CNN, Árboles de Decisión y FSM determinista) con datos de la NASA. Buscamos apoyo opcional en Ciencia de Datos, UI/UX o edición de video.
summary:
In microgravity, hot air does not rise. Flames form dim blue spheres or invisible cool flames (500–800 K) that defy Earth-based fire alarms. Built by two passionate engineers from Central America—combining Mechatronics & Control with Industrial Management—AERO-IGNIS SI is an open-source web observatory and engineering platform that turns 24 NASA Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI) combustion studies and 566 calibrated BASS-II, Saffire I–VI, and FLEX/CFI-G runs into actionable cabin fire-safety tools.

To address the challenge, the platform integrates three self-contained ML/DL engines: (1) TF-IDF/PCA/K-Means clustering, TOPSIS ranking, and DOI-grounded synthesis tailored to researchers, students, and managers; (2) a cabin flammability predictor pairing Damköhler/Péclet physics with RandomForest and GradientBoosting (78.49% 5-fold CV accuracy) plus forensic presets for Apollo 1, Apollo 13, Mir, and Artemis; and (3) an ONNX CNN and Decision Tree driving a fail-safe duct digital twin, alongside a NASA-STD-6001 FMEA matrix and Spinoff calculator.

This matters because safer pressurized habitats (ISS, Cygnus, Artemis) protect crews in orbit while tracing how space combustion science saves lives on Earth through NASA Spinoffs (9582, 9407, 9918, PFE).
details:
"Look at what happens when gravity disappears," says the Mechatronics & Control Engineer. "Hot gas stops rising. A flame turns into a quiet blue sphere—or keeps burning as an invisible cool flame between 500 and 800 Kelvin after looking extinguished."

"And in a closed habitat, physics alone isn't enough," replies the Industrial Management Engineer. "Apollo 1, Apollo 13, and Mir proved that cabin fire safety depends on materials, ventilation, detection, suppression, and human risk governance. NASA's PSI repository holds the experimental answers—our job is to make them usable."

We are two passionate engineers from Central America who built AERO-IGNIS SI because we believe our region has the talent and engineering discipline to contribute directly to global aerospace safety and technological progress.

---

1. WHAT DOES IT DO & HOW DOES IT WORK?

AERO-IGNIS SI is an interactive 7-module web platform (MIT license) scoped strictly to pressurized crewed habitats (ISS, Cygnus, Artemis lunar habitats) and terrestrial NASA Spinoffs:

- 01 · Virtual Museum & Glossary: Displays 6 NASA archive photos (0g flame, Apollo 1, Mir, BASS-II, Saffire, CIR) with a searchable plain-language glossary of orbital combustion physics.

- 02 · PSI Study Explorer & TOPSIS Ranking: Indexes 24 NASA PSI studies (DOIs 10.60555/psi-24 to psi-154) using TF-IDF + PCA + K-Means (4 clusters), multi-criteria TOPSIS/AHP prioritization, and deterministic TextRank synthesis adapted to Researcher, Student, and Industrial Manager profiles.

- 03 · Cabin Flammability Simulator & Forensic Presets: Computes dimensionless Damköhler (Da) and Péclet (Pe) numbers alongside RandomForestClassifier and GradientBoostingRegressor models trained on 566 calibrated physical runs, with one-click presets for Apollo 1, Apollo 13, Mir Kvant-1, and the Artemis Lunar Habitat (34% O2, 8.2 psi, 0.16g).

- 04 · Fail-Safe Duct Digital Twin: Combines a lightweight PyTorch-to-ONNX CNN (flame_cnn.onnx, 4 optical classes) and a sensor DecisionTreeClassifier (dT/dt, CO ppm, submicron aerosol <0.1 µm, airflow) inside a Deterministic FSM Controller (NORMAL -> PRE_ALERTA -> CONTENCION -> FALLA_SEGURA) with hysteresis, cool-flame re-ignition lockouts, and hardwired fail-safe transition if communication drops (comm_ok=False).

- 05 · NASA-STD-6001 FMEA & Dual-Use Spinoff Calculator: Evaluates 6 failure modes (FM-01..FM-06), models an ECLSS suppression selector (blocking CO2 when crew is present, prioritizing PFE fine water mist for auto-oxidizing cartridges, or E-FIELD for clean laminar flames), and quantifies terrestrial impact for NASA Spinoffs 9582, 9407, 9918, and PFE.

- 06 · Engineering Blueprints: Presents conceptual mechanical duct designs (250 × 250 × 600 mm), 24 VDC hardwired interlock schematics, and microcontroller sensor-conditioning concepts alongside the 10 primary NASA challenge resources.

- 07 · Methodology & Open Downloads: Publishes training pipelines, Mermaid architecture diagrams, datasets, and all 5 SHA-256-verified model artifacts (368.9 KB total).

2. WHAT BENEFITS DOES IT HAVE?

- Turns scattered orbital experiments into audience-appropriate insights with real, traceable DOIs (10.60555/...).

- Enables rapid "what-if" atmospheric testing (O2%, pressure, airflow, gravity, material thickness) and forensic replay of historical cabin fires.

- Quantifies risk mitigation (FMEA NPR reduction from 1901 to 134, -92.95%) and terrestrial firefighter/industrial benefits.

- Runs self-contained, lightweight models locally or in the cloud with SHA-256 verification and offline resilience.

3. WHAT IS THE INTENDED IMPACT OF THE PROJECT?

- Space & Education: Lower the barrier for students, researchers, and safety engineers—including across Latin America and Central America—to explore microgravity combustion physics and habitat fire safety using real NASA data.

- Earth Dual-Use: Demonstrate how orbital fire research directly strengthens terrestrial safety through lighter SCBA tanks (Spinoff 9582), early submicron smoke detection (9407), flame-resistant gear (9918), and clean fine water mist suppression (PFE).

4. WHAT TOOLS, CODING LANGUAGES, HARDWARE, OR SOFTWARE DID YOU USE?

- Software & ML/DL: Python 3.12, FastAPI, Pydantic v2, NumPy, scikit-learn (RandomForest, GradientBoosting, DecisionTree, TF-IDF, PCA, K-Means), PyTorch (training) -> ONNX Runtime (inference), Uvicorn, HTML5/CSS3/Vanilla JS/SVG, pytest (97 automated unit and integration tests), Google Colab (T4 notebook), GitHub, and Render.

- Engineering & Hardware Design Concepts: SolidWorks (bench-scale test duct CAD concept), EPLAN Electric P8 (24 VDC fail-safe interlock schematic concept), and Proteus ISIS (ESP32 and sensor-conditioning circuit concept).

- Super Intelligence (SI) Disclosure: AI coding and writing assistants were used during development for code scaffolding, debugging, documentation structuring, and translation/editing under human engineering verification and automated testing.

5. HOW IS YOUR PROJECT CREATIVE?

We united two distinct engineering perspectives—Mechatronics & Control and Industrial Management—into a single, cohesive observatory that bridges historical spaceflight storytelling, interactive physics-ML simulation, a fail-safe digital twin, and industrial FMEA/Spinoff economics. Using a short narrative dialogue framing, we make counter-intuitive zero-gravity fire behavior intuitive for students while preserving exact equations and DOIs for researchers.

6. WHAT FACTORS DID YOUR TEAM CONSIDER? (HONESTY & SCOPE)

- Strict Domain Boundary: Scoped strictly to pressurized crewed habitats and terrestrial Spinoffs; rocket engines and propulsion systems are excluded.

- Scientific Honesty (Real Data vs. Simulation): Model 1 achieves 78.49% 5-fold cross-validation accuracy across 566 calibrated physical runs (256 extinguished vs. 310 sustained propagation), reflecting real physical ambiguity near microgravity flammability limits. Model 2 achieves 100.0% only on our synthetic simulator (180 optical 64×64 frames and 600 sensor readings with controlled noise σ = 0.035), verifying mathematical and FSM logic—not flight readiness. Raw NASA OSDR video archives (~255.77 GB) are impractical for live browser streaming; flight deployment would require retraining on full OSDR imagery and formal NASA-STD-6001 hardware qualification.

- Hardware Prototype Status: SolidWorks, and KiCAD designs are conceptual/bench-scale engineering blueprints, not flight-certified hardware.

- Security & Data Integrity: Implemented Pydantic extra="forbid" validation, IP rate limiting, 16 KB payload limits, SSRF-allowlisted OSDR access with offline fallback, and mandatory SHA-256 verification against manifest.sha256.json before loading any model.

Live Platform: https://nasa-flame-in-freefal.onrender.com/

Source Code (MIT): https://github.com/Joshua-Sotomayor/NASA-flame-in-freefal
